clue.text: No high-living individual asks for minced fish

parts.note: minced meat has been put through a grinder, that is ground
the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone of modest means orders a fishcake made from minced fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A groundling was a spectator who stood in the cheap pit of an Elizabethan theatre, so hardly one living high; 'asks for' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundlings stood on the ground floor of the playhouse, the poorest audience members, the opposite of lofty living.

clue.text: Her Majesty's place in Canada

explanation.surface: Where the Queen goes when she visits Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, as in the royal signature; it is also the capital city of Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Gaunt ramblers in ramshackle hut given no guidance

indicators.note: one rearranged group of letters is placed in the other
a ramshackle hut is tumbledown, so its letters fall into disorder
the word Gaunt rambles, wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: Thin hikers holed up in a tumbledown shed have nobody to show them the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ramshackle' turns HUT into U...HT, and 'ramblers' turns GAUNT into NTAUG, which goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught has received no instruction or teaching.

clue.text: Not at all happy after a visit to the hairdresser?

definitions.text: after a visit to the hairdresser?

explanation.surface: A customer leaves the salon miserable with the haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the word as DIS- plus TRESSED: having had one's tresses (locks of hair) removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Distressed means upset and anguished; humorously, it also means relieved of one's tresses, or hair.

clue.text: Enliven much-liked feature of the church

parts.note: something popular or fashionable is said to be in
the tall pointed steeple top on a church tower

explanation.surface: A popular church steeple brightens up a village.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is to fill with spirit or animate, to stir into life.

clue.text: Rook or some other bird

explanation.surface: A rook, or perhaps a different kind of bird altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the crow, but here it is the verb meaning to cheat or swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To gull someone is to dupe or swindle them, just as to rook does; a gull is also a seabird.

clue.text: "Ever let the fancy roam, — never is at home" (Keats).

definitions.text: "Ever let the fancy roam, — never is at home" (Keats).

parts.words: "Ever let the fancy roam, — never is at home" (Keats).
parts.note: the opening lines of Keats's poem Fancy, with the missing word being the noun that names enjoyment or delight

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Keats's poem about letting the imagination wander.
explanation.walkthrough: The full lines read: 'Ever let the Fancy roam, / Pleasure never is at home'; the missing word is the one Keats says lives abroad, never in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap is filled by Keats's own word for delight or enjoyment, which he says always lies elsewhere.

clue.text: Green is to cut a rosy write-up he's promoting

indicators.note: the green piece and is slice into the middle of the other letters
in a down clue, writing a word up means setting it bottom to top, so rosy is read backwards

parts.note: rosy means red in colour
vert is the heraldic term for green
taken as written

explanation.surface: An environmentalist slashes a glowing review written about the product being pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write-up' turns RED into DER, giving A + DER; VERT + IS cuts it as AD/VERTIS/ER. Vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone promoting a product or service through public notices is an advertiser.

clue.text: French article about a youngster in need of clothing

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article meaning a
c, short for circa, means about
a lad is a boy or young fellow

explanation.surface: A French piece about a boy who needs something to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclad means naked, wearing no clothes, so its wearer needs some.

clue.text: Exceptionally self-conscious people

parts.note: read not as shy people but as those intensely conscious of their own self, always thinking of me first

explanation.surface: Painfully awkward people who feel everyone is watching them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'self-conscious' usually means embarrassed; here it means taken up with oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred, conceited people are wholly absorbed in themselves.

clue.text: Fence gives friend odd ideas

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend

indicators.note: odd ideas are strange ones, so the letters of ideas are put into a strange order

explanation.surface: A fence-building pal comes up with peculiar notions.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence of wooden stakes or railings, often defensive.

clue.text: Having written hurried note, made a phone-call

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to hurry
G is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: After jotting down a quick message, someone telephoned.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rung someone means to have telephoned them.

clue.text: The opposition's dubious ancestries

indicators.note: dubious ancestries are questionable ones, so the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: The opposition party's family trees are of questionable origin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's 's stands for 'is', linking opposition to its anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is opposition, especially the organised kind that fights an occupying force.

clue.text: Peerless area of London? Far from it!

definitions.text: Peerless area of London? Far from it!

parts.words: Peerless area of London? Far from it!
parts.note: read peerless literally as without a noble lord; far from lacking one, this London district's name contains a peer and his court

explanation.surface: A London district without equal, or not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a district in west London; an earl is a peer, so its name is anything but peer-less.
explanation.definitionFit: The district's name is literally the court of an earl, a member of the British peerage.

clue.text: Plane pronounced quiet — welcome that

parts.note: spoke means uttered or pronounced
sh is the call for silence
ave is the Latin greeting hail or welcome

explanation.surface: An aircraft was described as quiet, and that was well received.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft but is the carpenter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokeshave is a small two-handled woodworking plane for shaping curved pieces such as wheel spokes.

clue.text: A quarter of the quiz will be most undemanding

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
taken as written
a test is a quiz or examination

explanation.surface: One section of the general knowledge quiz will be the easiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Softest means least hard or demanding, the easiest.

clue.text: The Queen, perhaps, has her countenance on the programme

parts.note: the countenance is a person's face
a card is a printed programme, as at a race meeting

explanation.surface: The monarch's portrait appears in the printed programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen in a pack of cards is one of the picture cards along with king and jack.

clue.text: She entertains those odd characters with a certain craft

indicators.note: the characters of the word those are made odd, put out of order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a particular kind of vessel

explanation.surface: A party-giver welcomes strange guests with particular skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who receives and looks after guests is a hostess.

clue.text: Jack goes off it when without money

parts.note: milk turns when it goes off, going sour
P for penny or pence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man walks off the job when he finds there is no money in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack is a device for turning a roasting spit; 'when' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit was a person, dog or mechanical jack employed to rotate meat roasting over a fire.

clue.text: Delayed acquiring further equipment for the new baby

indicators.note: the word for delayed acquires another, taking it inside

parts.note: late means delayed or behind time
yet means still more or further, as in yet another

explanation.surface: Late with gathering more kit for the newborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the set of clothes, bedding and other items prepared for a newborn infant.

clue.text: Mediocre judge is after support

indicators.note: the word for judge comes after the word for support

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: An average referee wants backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means of inferior quality, ordinary at best.

clue.text: Erect back

explanation.surface: Stand up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to raise upright or build; the rear is the back or hind part.

clue.text: Having put in an appearance, is near collapse

indicators.note: the words is near collapse into a heap and reform

explanation.surface: Someone shows up but is on the point of fainting.
explanation.definitionFit: Arisen means come into being or appeared, as a problem that has arisen.

clue.text: Exact bill a minister presented

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is a clergyman, a minister of the church

explanation.surface: A vicar presents a precise invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct in every detail, precise.

clue.text: A tale constantly re-read absorbs him

indicators.note: the words of the phrase absorb the name, holding it within them

explanation.surface: Someone reads a story again and again and is gripped by it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'tALE Constantly'; 're-read' is surface only, not a reversal. 'him' defines a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a man's given name, a short form of Alexander, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: Some retired reverential holy man — a monk

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the word for some is read backwards

parts.note: part means some, a portion
pi is short for pious, reverential
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A partly withdrawn, devout religious figure is a monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trappist is a monk of the strict Cistercian order of La Trappe, noted for silence.

clue.text: An enchanting woman, about fifty, in society

indicators.note: the enchantress goes about, surrounding, the number

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of Greek myth who turned Odysseus's men into pigs
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A charming woman of around fifty moves in high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enchanting' looks like charming but means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a social group or set, as in moving in exalted circles.

clue.text: Sort of fruit raised by the old miner

explanation.surface: A kind of fruit grown by a former coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is from the American folk song 'Oh My Darling Clementine', whose heroine was the daughter of a miner, forty-niner.
explanation.definitionFit: A clementine is a small seedless citrus like a tangerine; in the song, the girl of that name was brought up by her mining father.
